patch.value: Gated sync still refuses GitHub #134 import ownership across two closed PM records

Tracks gh:unbraind/pm-linear#198 (filed 2026-11-01, missed by the blind issue watch). The scheduled gated sync on main still fails the ownership preflight ('GitHub issue #134 has multiple existing owners'): the imported issue item carries the gh: tag and another closed record (pm-linear-ldqw) starts its description with the same source issue URL, which the identity contract treats as a competing ownership declaration. Latest failing run 41297539843 (2026-11-01T10:27Z); the failure repeats daily. Reconcile exactly one import owner with supported PM operations while preserving both records' knowledge, relationships and durable history (reword the competing description or convert the claim to a structured relationship); keep the fail-closed guard.

value.text: Duplicate #134 ownership reconciled, plus a second masked blocker found and fixed. (1) The competing record no longer declares GitHub ownership: its description no longer leads with 'GitHub issue <url>' (the URL reference is preserved in prose), a related dependency now links it to the imported record, and its status stays closed. The imported record keeps the gh: tag and github_url as sole owner. (2) The gated dry-run then refused with '1 conflicting target(s)': one feature record carried gh: tags for issues #191 and #193 as well as PR #189, so two importable issues resolved to a single item. Those two identity tags were removed (the PR #189 provenance tag stays; the relationship is documented in a comment on that record) so the import creates dedicated records for #191 and #193. Measurement — before: failing run https://github.com/unbraind/pm-linear/actions/runs/41297539843 (2026-11-01T10:27Z, 'GitHub issue #134 has multiple existing owners'). After: the same gated dry-run the scheduled workflow runs (pm-github 2026.10.28 as pinned by the reusable workflow) passes against this branch's tracker: fetched 8, planned 8, import 3, update 5, skip 0, provenance-indexed 8, #134 resolves uniquely to the imported record via provenance-tag. The command is linked as a passing test; its pm-test receipt runs in pm's isolated seeded workspace, so the reconciliation numbers here come from the direct dry-run against this checkout. GitHub API budget was checked before measuring (core remaining above the 1500 floor). Guard unchanged; item stays open for orchestrator close after merge.

## Current hosted failure and canonical ownership
At default commit `133914ec3f7b39c00ae2434f138c004540d9e5a2`, the [gated sync job](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-linear/actions/runs/41297539843/job/124821446773) fails during `pm github import unbraind/pm-linear --state all --atomic --gate --dry-run --with-comments`:

> GitHub issue #134 has multiple existing owners; import plan is not idempotent. No item was written for this issue.

The latest same-head sync check was still failed when refreshed at 2026-11-01 10:57 UTC. Canonical tracker inspection finds two closed records referring to the same source issue:
- [pm-linear-github-18076be0368a-134](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-linear/blob/133914ec3f7b39c00ae2434f138c004540d9e5a2/.agents/pm/issues/pm-linear-github-18076be0368a-134.toon) has the explicit `gh:unbraind/pm-linear#134` tag and imported source description.
- [pm-linear-ldqw](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-linear/blob/133914ec3f7b39c00ae2434f138c004540d9e5a2/.agents/pm/issues/pm-linear-ldqw.toon) starts its description with the same GitHub issue URL and retains implementation acceptance/evidence.

Expected: one unambiguous importer owner for #134, while both records' useful knowledge, relationships and durable history remain intact. Actual: the guarded import refuses the ambiguous plan, blocking scheduled documentation synchronization. The refusal is appropriate; this is not evidence of data loss or a reason to weaken the guard.

## Acceptance and limits
- Reconcile importer ownership using supported PM operations, retaining both records and their provenance/history or performing an explicitly verified preservation migration.
- Keep implementation/source-issue relationships without a second competing importer identity.
- Demonstrate dry-run and applied import followed by an identical repeat produce no duplicate owner and no unintended item/history changes.
- Keep atomicity and privacy gates enabled.

This report combines exact hosted failure with static canonical records; no live import, tracker mutation or local implementation was run. Checked all 197 current all-status GitHub items and 114 canonical PM `.toon` records before filing; no matching ownership-remediation issue found.
